items.text: Axios (1 week ago — the most complete deal architecture confirmed): The agreement the US and Iran are close to signing involves: (1) A 60-day ceasefire extension. (2) During the 60-day period, the Strait of Hormuz would be open with no tolls and Iran would agree to clear the mines it deployed in the strait to let ships pass freely. (3) In exchange, the US would lift its blockade on Iranian ports and issue some sanctions waivers to allow Iran to sell oil freely. (4) Negotiations on curbing Iran's nuclear program held during the 60-day period. A US official acknowledged lifting the port blockade and sanctions waivers would be a boon to Iran's economy, but said it would also give significant relief to the global oil market. The official said the faster the Iranians clear the mines and let shipping resume, the faster the blockade will be lifted. Both Trump and the mediators indicated the deal could be announced on Sunday (May 25) — it was not. The deal remains unsigned but the framework is confirmed by multiple sources now. This is the closest to a signed deal that the 92-day war has produced.

Camp David meeting = the most senior-level Iran deal review of the war. If Trump signed at Camp David: the deal would have been announced Wednesday May 28. No announcement came — meaning either Trump did not sign at Camp David or the meeting extended deliberations. As of June 1 Monday 9 AM: Trump has still not signed the MOU.

military.t: AXIOS EXCLUSIVE CONFIRMED: 60-Day MOU Details — Hormuz NO TOLLS + Iran Clears Mines + US Lifts Port Blockade + Sanctions Waivers + Nuclear Talks.
military.d: Axios (1 week ago — exclusive, verified by multiple sources): The agreement the US and Iran are close to signing involves: (1) 60-day ceasefire extension. (2) Hormuz open with no tolls — Iran clears mines it deployed. (3) US lifts blockade on Iranian ports. (4) US issues sanctions waivers for Iran to sell oil freely. (5) Nuclear negotiations held during 60-day period. A US official acknowledged the port blockade lifting and sanctions waivers would boost Iran's economy — but said it would also give "significant relief to the global oil market." "The faster the Iranians clear the mines and let shipping resume, the faster the blockade will be lifted." This incentive structure means Iran has maximum motivation to de-mine quickly once MOU is signed. The Axios details have been verified by other sources close to the talks. Iran has not confirmed details — but Tehran has indicated a deal is close. Both Trump and mediators indicated deal could be announced on Sunday May 25 — it was not. The framework is confirmed. The signature is not.

military.t: TRUMP REVIEWING — HAS NOT SIGNED. Camp David Cabinet Meeting Held. NBC: Had Not Signed After US-Iran Traded Attacks.
military.d: NBC News (2 days ago) and CNBC (5 days ago) confirmed: Trump was reviewing the latest version of a potential agreement but had not signed after the two countries traded attacks. A White House official confirmed to CNBC that Trump and his Cabinet would meet at Camp David on Wednesday May 28 to discuss the deal. Camp David = most senior-level Iran deal review of the war. No deal was announced following Camp David — meaning either Trump withheld signature or deliberations continued. As of June 1, 9 AM IST: no confirmed Trump MOU signature. The remaining obstacles as Trump sees them: nuclear conditions (four conditions confirmed by CNBC) — though Axios suggests the framework bridges conditions 1-3 cleanly. Condition 4 (US destroys buried uranium) likely a Phase 2 verification item. Trump's political incentive to sign: US gas prices down 14 cents (biggest drop since 2008). Trump's political risk of signing: Netanyahu opposition if nuclear not addressed upfront.

military.t: AXIOS DEAL SIGNIFICANCE FOR INDIA: No-Toll Hormuz + Sanctions Waivers = Rs 3L Cr Annual Saving. Bessent License = India Refiners Buy Iranian Crude.
military.d: The Axios deal details have direct and quantified India implications: (1) Hormuz open with no tolls: PGSA toll system dismantled in deal language — India LPG, fertiliser, crude transit without IRGC fees. (2) Iran clears mines: Cooper 90% cleared already. Remaining 10%: 2-4 weeks. Full VLCC transit: 3-6 weeks post-signing. (3) US sanctions waivers for Iran oil sales: Bessent's "energy-vulnerable countries" general license applies directly. India refiners (IOC, BPCL, HPCL, Reliance) can purchase Iranian crude under sanctions waivers. At $82 Brent post-deal: annual import bill saving approximately Rs 3 lakh crore vs $126 April peak. OMC: petrol profitable at $82. Diesel under-recovery Rs 8-12/L. Potential petrol price reversal in 30-60 days. (4) Kharif fertiliser: Gulf sourcing fully viable — Gulf produces 30% of global urea. No tolls + mines cleared = fertiliser carriers transit freely.

military.t: UBS: "Extremely Low" Vessel Traffic. Brent $92 = Deal Priced, Not Done. Hochstein Reality Persists.
military.d: CNBC (17 hours ago) confirmed UBS note: crude loadings inside the Gulf remain "extremely low." There is still "little evidence" of any short-term improvement in vessel traffic or energy flows. Brent $92 = deal expectation already largely priced. When MOU signed + de-mining begins: Brent target $80-85 (limited additional downside already priced). But the operational India benefit — LPG, fertiliser, crude carriers actually transiting Hormuz — is what matters for the real economy. Hochstein's verdict (Day 90, confirmed): "No matter what happens, Iranians control Hormuz for the foreseeable future." This means: even post-deal, India's Hormuz posture involves PGSA-style coordination (under a different name post-deal). The Axios deal papers over the sovereignty language. The operational reality of Iranian Hormuz management persists. India must build permanent IRGC coordination infrastructure.

assessment.body:
Monday 9:00 AM IST. June 1, 2026. Day 92. Week 14. The war enters its fourth month with the deal confirmed on paper and unsigned in practice.

THE AXIOS DEAL — WHAT'S CONFIRMED
60-day ceasefire extension.
Hormuz: open with NO TOLLS.
Iran: clears all mines it deployed.
US: lifts blockade on Iranian ports.
US: issues sanctions waivers for Iran to sell oil freely.
Nuclear: negotiations held during 60-day period.
Incentive structure: faster Iran clears mines → faster US lifts blockade.
Iran's economic demand (sell oil freely) met in Phase 1.
Trump's operational demand (Hormuz without tolls, mines cleared) met in Phase 1.
Nuclear: Phase 2 — 60 days to negotiate.

WHY TRUMP HASN'T SIGNED
Camp David Cabinet meeting held Wednesday May 28.
No announcement followed.
Possible reasons: Netanyahu pressure on nuclear upfront conditions, Iran's version of MOU (Iran+Oman manage Hormuz) vs White House ("complete fabrication"), Trump's four conditions — especially condition 4 (US destroys buried uranium) — not yet in writing.
The Axios bridge suggests conditions 1-3 are met. Condition 4 is the Phase 2 verification item.

THE MARKET-REALITY GAP
Brent $92 = deal expectation almost fully priced.
UBS: crude loadings "extremely low" — no actual improvement.
IRGC: still firing warning shots at vessels without coordination.
When Trump signs: limited additional Brent downside ($80-85 target).
The real India benefit: operational — ships actually moving.

HOCHSTEIN'S PERMANENT VERDICT
"No matter what happens, Iranians control Hormuz. Doesn't even matter what the deal says."
The PGSA 'controlled maritime zone' graphic (May 20) remains published.
The IRGC coordination requirement remains operational.
The deal papers over the language. The architecture persists.
India's permanent Hormuz posture: case-by-case, ship-by-ship coordination.

INDIA'S WEEK 14 AGENDA
1. Haji Ali MEA protest: file Monday — 17 days overdue.
2. Bessent sanctions waivers: engage Treasury — India refiners apply.
3. PGSA applications: submit — de-mining still requires coordination.
4. Kharif fertiliser: order now — delivery within de-mining window.
5. Monitor Trump signature: the single event that changes India's energy reality.

VERDICT: Week 14 opens with the deal fully described by Axios, confirmed by multiple sources, and unsigned by Trump. The framework bridges every gap that has existed in the 92-day war — Hormuz without tolls, mines cleared, Iran's economy reopened, nuclear deferred to Phase 2. The only question is whether Trump signs it. His political incentive is maximum (gas prices at 2008 drop levels). His political risk is Netanyahu. His strategic leverage is time — "time is on Washington's side." For India, the calculation is different: every day without the signature costs Rs 400+ crore in import bill excess, drains OMC balance sheets, and keeps 280 Indian seafarers in the Gulf zone. The deal is done on paper. India needs it done in ink.
